issue_context.title: GraalVM native image kerberos authentication issue: failed to store/retrieve AccessControlContext to/from stack
comments:
I am looking into this. 
There are several ways this issue can be worked around so I'm going to do run tests in order to be as compatible with JVM as possible atm.

Update: I'm going deep into the rabbit hole with this. It seems that our Thread implementation doesn't respect passed `AccessControlContext` which manifests in all kinds of bugs. I'm currently trying to remove as much substitutions as I can which should not only fix this bug, but privilege checking tests as well.
@zcui001 can you check if linked pull request (#3098) fixes the issue for you?
We are using GraalVM native 22.3.1 Java 17 EE and are still seeing this issue when using native-image

review_comments: Please mark as many substitutions as possible as `JDK11OrEarlier`, since JDK 16 already has these methods implemented in Java.

Problem is that JDK16's implementation assumes that `getStackAccessControlContext` can easily access method locals from `javaVFrame` to extract `context` and `caller`. Relevant code from Hotspot's `jvm.cpp`:
```
      javaVFrame *priv = vfst.asJavaVFrame();       // executePrivileged
      StackValueCollection* locals = priv->locals();
      StackValue* ctx_sv = locals->at(1); // AccessControlContext context
      StackValue* clr_sv = locals->at(2); // Class<?> caller
```
In order to avoid that - since AFAIK there is no nice and easy way to achieve that - I opted for Espresso approach by implementing parallel stack which is `FastThreadLocal`. Negative side of that approach is that we need to substitute `doPrivileged` even on JDK15+.
The parallel stack approach is fine. But still, the `doPrivileged` methods themselves do not need to be substituted anymore on JDK 16.
